command:
set -euo pipefail
cd /tmp

echo "== verify staged reads against their pinned sha256 =="
{ printf '%s  %s\n' 1198ed07e41fdf6f53710dfe4eee376d978e1bf61f0d9dcdd8b7ec2ce7c5432e ERR188026_sub_1.fq.gz
  printf '%s  %s\n' 6104ee4641702156ce3f5330b750db6fd461e597de43bb280158bc751a7e120a ERR188026_sub_2.fq.gz
} > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

tar -xf star-index.tar
rm -f star-index.tar
test -s idx/SA

echo "== STAR align: 200,000 read pairs vs the chr20 index =="
STAR --genomeDir idx --readFilesIn ERR188026_sub_1.fq.gz ERR188026_sub_2.fq.gz \
     --readFilesCommand zcat --runThreadN 8 --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate \
     --quantMode GeneCounts --outFileNamePrefix aln_

# ---- smoke check ----
# READ THE BANDS BEFORE THE NUMBERS. Uniquely-mapped is ~6.7%, and 92.7% of reads
# come back "unmapped: too short". That is the expected, correct result for a
# whole-transcriptome library aligned against ONE chromosome: most reads simply have
# no home in the reference, and "too short" is STAR's catch-all for a read that
# fails the minimum-mapped-length filter. It is not a broken run. See README.
gv() { awk -F'\t' -v k="$1" 'index($1, k) { gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", $2); print $2; exit }' aln_Log.final.out; }
INPUT=$(gv 'Number of input reads')
UNIQ=$(gv 'Uniquely mapped reads number')
UPCT=$(gv 'Uniquely mapped reads %')
MULTI=$(gv 'Number of reads mapped to multiple loci')
SPLICED=$(gv 'Number of splices: Total')
ANNOT=$(gv 'Number of splices: Annotated (sjdb)')
BAMBYTES=$(wc -c < aln_Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam)
GENEROWS=$(wc -l < aln_ReadsPerGene.out.tab | tr -d ' ')
GENESHIT=$(awk 'NR>4 && $2>=1' aln_ReadsPerGene.out.tab | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
SPECIAL=$(awk 'NR<=4 && $1 ~ /^N_/' aln_ReadsPerGene.out.tab | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
UPCT_NUM=${UPCT%\%}

{
  echo "input_reads          $INPUT     want exactly 200000"
  echo "uniquely_mapped      $UNIQ      want   4000..40000   (observed 13346)"
  echo "uniquely_mapped_pct  $UPCT      want    2.0..20.0    (observed 6.67 - see README)"
  echo "multi_loci           $MULTI     want    100..10000   (observed  1160)"
  echo "splices_total        $SPLICED   want    500..20000   (observed  2612)"
  echo "splices_annotated    $ANNOT     want > 500           (observed  2139)"
  echo "bam_bytes            $BAMBYTES  want > 200000        (observed 2284962)"
  echo "readspergene_rows    $GENEROWS  want   1900..2100    (observed 1976 = 4 + 1972 chr20 genes)"
  echo "genes_with_a_read    $GENESHIT  want    100..1500    (observed   423)"
  echo "readspergene_headers $SPECIAL   want exactly 4       (N_unmapped/N_multimapping/N_noFeature/N_ambiguous)"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
cat aln_Log.final.out

test "$INPUT"    -eq 200000
test "$UNIQ"     -ge 4000
test "$UNIQ"     -le 40000
test "$MULTI"    -ge 100
test "$MULTI"    -le 10000
test "$SPLICED"  -ge 500
test "$SPLICED"  -le 20000
test "$ANNOT"    -gt 500
test "$BAMBYTES" -gt 200000
test "$GENEROWS" -ge 1900
test "$GENEROWS" -le 2100
test "$GENESHIT" -ge 100
test "$GENESHIT" -le 1500
test "$SPECIAL"  -eq 4
awk -v p="$UPCT_NUM" 'BEGIN{ if (p >= 2.0 && p <= 20.0) exit 0; print "unique% " p " outside band"; exit 1 }'
# A sorted BAM starts with the BGZF magic bytes; this is the cheapest real check
# that the file is a BAM and not a truncated write, with no samtools in this image.
test "$(head -c 4 aln_Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')" = "1f8b0804"
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
